items.actClause:
AN ACT authorizing the city of Albany to alienate certain lands used as
parkland and to dedicate certain other lands as parklands
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5616

SPONSOR: BRESLIN
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act authorizing the city of Albany to alienate
certain lands used as parkland and to dedicate certain other lands as
parklands

 
PURPOSE:

To alienate a portion of Lincoln Park to allow for the construction and
maintenance of a new underground pipe through Lincoln Park to Morton
Avenue. These lands in conjunction with the lands previously alienated
for the construction of the screening and disinfection facility will
define the limits of total park lands which need to be alienated for the
Project.

Under the legislation, consistent with other requirements of law, the
city of Albany will dedicate an amount equal to or greater than the fair
market value of the parklands being discontinued towards the acquisition
of new parklands and/or capital improvements to existing park and recre-
ational facilities.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 authorizes the City of Albany to alienate the parkland for the
purpose of the provision of underground piping through Lincoln Park in
connection with the disinfection and floatables control project, and
associated infrastructure, also known as the Beaver Creek Clean River
Project (screening and disinfection satellite treatment facility).

Section 2 requires the city of Albany to dedicate an amount equal to or
greater than the fair market value of the parklands being discontinued
towards the acquisition of new parklands and/or capital improvements to
existing park and recreational facilities.

Section 3 describes the relevant parkland and specifies acreage and
borders.

Section 4 requires the city of Albany, if it received any funding
support or assistance from the federal government for the purchase,
maintenance or improvement of the parklands set forth in section three
of this act, the discontinuance and alienation of such parkland author-
ized by the provisions of this act shall not occur until the city of
Albany has complied with any federal requirements, pertaining to the
alienation or conversion of such parklands, including satisfying the
secretary of the interior that the alienation or conversion complies
with all conditions which the secretary of the interior deems necessary
to assure the substitution of other lands shall be equivalent in fair
market value and usefulness to the lands being alienated or converted.

Section 5 provides that the act shall take effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The Lincoln Park Clean River Project, part of the Albany Pool Combined
Sewer Overflow Long Term Control Plan, is required to be constructed
under an effective Order on Consent between the Albany Water Board and
Department of Environmental Conservation. The Project provides for the
screening and disinfection of wet weather flows for the Beaver Creek
Sewer District, and is intended to improve the water quality of the
Hudson River.

As part of the development for the Project, the Albany Water Board has
conducted an extensive public education and outreach program.  In order
to address public concerns relative. to the removal and storage of solid
materials in the park, a partnership between the Albany Water Board and
the Albany County Water Purification District (ACWPD) was formed. Under
this partnership, solid materials which are screened in the park will be
conveyed directly to the ACWPD South Treatment Plant where they will be
removed and processed. The conveyance of the screened materials requires
a new direct connection from the proposed screening and disinfection
facility to the Albany County Hudson River Interceptor. The selected
routing for this new connection will run through Lincoln Park to Morton
Avenue and then along South Hawk Street where it will connect to an
existing pipe on Third Avenue and ultimately the County's interceptor
sewer.  In addition, provisions have been incorporated into the Project
for improved circulation of traffic and parking; along with the relo-
cation of the existing access drive between Delaware Avenue and Dr.
Martin Luther King, Jr. Boulevard.

The proposed modifications to the Project will require that additional
parklands to be alienated. Areas impacted due to the improved traffic
circulation and parking, as well as the relocated access drive, are
defined in the Phase 1A map and description. Areas required to construct
and maintain the new underground pipe connection through Lincoln Park to
Morton Avenue are designated in the Phase 2 map and description. These
lands in conjunction with the lands previously alienated for the
construction of the screening and disinfection facility will define the
limits of total park lands which need to be alienated for the Project.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

No cost to the state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
